deep.reconstruction:
The page is headed 'Lemniscata', with columns 'Arc.' and 'Rad. v' (radius vector). It is the start of a table of the lemniscatic sine.

Setup (modern notation, my reconstruction):
- For the lemniscate r^2 = cos 2θ, the arc length from the node to the point with radius vector r is s = ∫_0^r dt/√(1−t^4).
- The inverse function r = sl(s) is the lemniscatic sine.
- The full quadrant arc is ϖ/2 = ∫_0^1 dt/√(1−t^4) = 1.3110287771…
- Gauss divides this quadrant into 90 'lemniscatic degrees', exactly as with the circle. The argument 'Arc' = n therefore means s = n·ϖ/180, where ϖ/180 = 0.0145669864…
- The second column gives sl(n·ϖ/180) to 7 decimals, with the leading decimal point omitted (0145670 = 0.0145670).

How the values can be obtained: for small s the Taylor series suffices,
sl s = s − s^5/10 + s^9/120 − (4390848/13!)·s^13 + …
Examples:
- n = 10: s = 0.14566986, s^5/10 = 0.00000656, so sl = 0.1456633.
- n = 15: s = 0.21850480, s^5/10 = 0.00004981, so sl = 0.2184550.

The single entry at Arc 30 is 4354205, i.e. sl(ϖ/6) = 0.4354205. This is presumably an algebraically computed anchor point (my inference). Since ϖ/6 = ϖ/2 − ϖ/3,
sl(ϖ/6) = cl(ϖ/3) = √((1−sl²(ϖ/3))/(1+sl²(ϖ/3))), with sl²(ϖ/3) = √(2√3−3).
This gives √(0.31875/1.68125) = 0.4354205. The series to the s^13 term gives the same value.

Structure of the argument grid:
- step 1 for 0–10;
- step 0.5 for 10–20;
- step 0.2 for 20–36;
- step 1/8 from 36 to 41 on this page (written 36^1 … 36^7, 37, 37^1 …, superscripts = eighths), continuing on the next page to about 45 7/8;
- then tenths (45,0 … 45,9, 46,0 …).
The target is evidently at least 45 = ϖ/4, the half-quadrant. The rest of the quadrant would follow from sl(ϖ/2 − u) = cl u = √((1−sl²u)/(1+sl²u)) (my inference).

Only arcs 0–15.5 and 30 are filled in. The previous page holds a rougher 5–6-digit marginal draft of the same column.
